thread_analysis.thread_summary: IDEAL Co. BLE product registration thread (2343 lines, 6 messages). Customer uses Nordic SoftDevice v6.1.1. Three key technical/administrative questions answered: (1) optional non-Bluetooth accessories (plastic cover) are excluded from SIG registration scope; (2) third-party payment of SIG Declaration Fee is acceptable, but the SIG Invoice must be obtained by the registrant company using their own account — QN is non-transferable; (3) FX rate for proxy payment is the TTS rate at end of the month before formal quote issuance; (4) antenna data sheet for Compliance Folder can be a page from the BLE module spec sheet if it contains a radiation gain characteristics diagram. Thread also documents the full registration flow: Step 1 (order + payment), Step 2 (Allion registers, 1-3 business days), Step 3 (Compliance Folder with 4 documents). Note: customer was warned that the SIG Invoice must be obtained under the registrant's SIG account — a critical instruction to prevent QN being issued to the wrong company.
all_questions_found: Does an optional non-Bluetooth plastic cover need to be included in the SIG registration?
When is the FX rate fixed for Allion-proxied USD wire transfer to SIG? Can a third party pay?
Can the antenna data sheet for the Compliance Folder be a page from the BLE module spec sheet?
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: The SIG Invoice / Qualification Number issuance rule is the highest-risk issue in this thread: the QN is issued to whichever company's SIG account obtained the Invoice. If Company B (the payer) logs in and gets the Invoice, Company B gets the QN — not Company A (the intended registrant). This is irreversible. Sakai proactively warned IDEAL about this rule.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: Three rules: (1) non-BT accessories excluded from registration scope; (2) QN follows the SIG account that obtains the Invoice — not the payer; TTS month-end rate applies for proxy payments; (3) antenna data sheet = radiation gain data required, format flexible.
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: The QN / Invoice misuse is catastrophic — if the wrong company obtains the Invoice, the QN is permanently issued to them and cannot be recovered. All other issues in this thread are minor documentation format questions.
thread_analysis.consulting_mistake: No mistakes — Sakai correctly flagged the Invoice/QN rule proactively without waiting for the customer to make the error.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: Always include the Invoice acquisition warning as a mandatory step in every SIG registration onboarding: 'Only the registrant company's SIG account holder should log in to obtain the Invoice.' This warning should be written into every registration guidance document sent to customers.
